name: incest

attributes.attribute: a mythic theme, with brother-sister unions read as creation myths
a figure whose sons were fathered, sources imply, by her brother Gwidion

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Incest is a Celtic mythic theme. Tales of a brother and sister joining were read as creation myths. At the start of time incest was the only way to people the world. Such unions appear in several Celtic myths. Arianhrod bore two sons when asked to prove her virginity by magic. Sources imply that her brother Gwidion fathered the children. King Arthur also had a child with his sister, the magical Morgause. These incestuous unions are used to argue that figures were once divine and later diminished into human form.

okr.objective: Document incest as a Celtic mythic theme.
key_results: Record the reading of incest tales as creation myths.
Note the Arianhrod and Gwidion union.
Note King Arthur's child with his sister Morgause.
